lead:
The federal government suspended 20 Civil Defence officers and the Niger State commandant over the deaths of 37 suspected illegal miners in custody, and NAFDAC confirmed high levels of methanol in the drinks blamed for 48 deaths in Ondo.

The day in brief: Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo said the suspensions would last until an independent investigation reports, as rights groups demanded transparency and Atiku Abubakar said the President owed Nigerians answers. NAFDAC said 182 cases had been recorded in Odigbo. Gunmen attacked a busy market in Mangu at nightfall, killing three people, and the Red Cross said more than 17,000 people separated by the Boko Haram conflict remain missing. With petrol above N1,400 a litre in parts of Abuja, the regulator said it cannot fix prices but opened channels to report abuse, President Tinubu urged a faster move to gas-powered vehicles, and Atiku called on him to cut fuel prices. Unity college teachers suspended their strike over the planned concession of King's College, and the Falconets prepared to meet Colombia in the U20 Women's World Cup quarter-final.

items.h: 20 NSCDC officers suspended over deaths of mining suspects
items.s: The Federal Government suspended 20 Civil Defence officers and the Niger State NSCDC commandant, Suberu Aniviye, pending an independent investigation into the deaths of 37 suspected illegal miners in the corps' custody, Interior Minister Olubunmi Tunji-Ojo said. The Campaign for Democracy asked the National Security Adviser to ensure an independent inquiry, and Atiku Abubakar said the President and two ministers owe Nigerians answers.

items.h: NAFDAC finds methanol in drinks linked to 48 Ondo deaths
items.s: NAFDAC confirmed high concentrations of methanol in locally made alcoholic and herbal mixtures linked to 48 deaths in Odigbo local government area, Ondo State. Director-General Mojisola Adeyeye said 182 cases had been recorded as of 17 September across several communities.

items.h: Gunmen kill three in Mangu market
items.s: Gunmen stormed a busy cash-crop and vegetable market in Mangu town at about 8.30pm on Friday, as traders and buyers were closing for the day, killing three people. Many others were injured by gunfire and in the stampede as people fled in different directions, residents said.

items.h: Red Cross says 17,000 people still missing in the North-East
items.s: More than 17,000 people separated from their families by the Boko Haram conflict in the North-East are still missing, the ICRC's spokesman Aliyu Dawobe said at the end of a training for journalists in Lagos. He said the figure was once over 24,000 but was reduced because the Red Cross lost contact with some families.

items.h: Regulator says it does not fix petrol prices
items.s: The NMDPRA said the Petroleum Industry Act does not allow it to fix pump prices in the deregulated market, while acknowledging the financial pressure caused by the latest rise in petrol prices. It opened dedicated channels for the public and industry to report exploitative pricing and fuel smuggling.

items.h: Tinubu urges CNG rollout as petrol tops N1,400
items.s: President Tinubu said Nigeria's exposure to global energy price shocks makes the move to alternative fuels such as compressed natural gas necessary, and urged a faster rollout. His remarks came as petrol pump prices passed N1,400 a litre in parts of Abuja.

items.h: Atiku calls on Tinubu to cut fuel prices
items.s: At a press conference in Abuja, Atiku Abubakar urged President Tinubu to cut the prices of petrol and diesel and use his government's remaining months to bring relief to families, workers, farmers and businesses. “Bola Tinubu should not be ashamed to do what is necessary to lower the price of petrol,” he said.

items.h: Mining pit collapse kills five in Taraba
items.s: A mining pit collapsed on Thursday at Mayo Kam in Bali local government area of Taraba. Early reports said more than 20 people were trapped, but police and eyewitnesses who joined the rescue said only five miners were in the pit; four or five died, and at least one was pulled out alive.

items.h: Benue police arrest 17 over mob attack on officers
items.s: Benue police said they arrested 17 people over a mob attack on officers at Adagi, Jato-Aka, in Kwande on 30 August, and rescued eight people. Commissioner Cletus Nwadiogbu told journalists in Makurdi that one of the injured officers is still alive but on life support in a hospital in Anambra State.

items.h: Military says 50 kidnap victims rescued in a week
items.s: Defence Headquarters said troops across all theatres rescued at least 50 kidnap victims and arrested several terrorists, collaborators and suspected kidnappers in offensive operations between 11 and 17 September.

items.h: Bandits kill local security commander in Kwara
items.s: Suspected bandits killed Agbeniga Taye, a commander of the local security outfit in Idofin-Ayekale, Oke-Ero local government area of Kwara, and abducted two residents when they invaded the community. Police had yet to confirm the attack.

items.h: Village head abducted in Kano
items.s: Gunmen abducted Alhaji Ahmad Yakubu Ahmad, village head of Aujarawar Alkali in Gezawa, Kano, when they stormed the community on Thursday night, said Mahi Isma'il, spokesman for the district head of Jogana.

items.h: Presidency and SEC plan to channel savings into capital market
items.s: The Presidency and the Securities and Exchange Commission unveiled plans to deepen the capital market and mobilise domestic savings towards the $1 trillion economy target. The SEC will introduce a National Savings Scheme backed by tax incentives, and Vice President Shettima is expected to endorse a new Nigerian Capital Market Master Plan.

items.h: NUPRC sets 31 October deadline for idle oil licences
items.s: The NUPRC said it will enforce the Petroleum Industry Act's “drill-or-drop” provisions and gave holders of non-performing licences, including winners of the 2020 marginal field round, until 31 October to report their status, explain what is delaying them and submit plans, or risk losing their acreage.

items.h: Falconets face Colombia in quarter-final
items.s: After beating England 3-0 in the round of 16, the Falconets prepared to face Colombia in the FIFA U20 Women's World Cup quarter-final in Łódź, chasing their first semi-final in 12 years. They beat Colombia 1-0 in the 2010 semi-final, and coach Moses Aduku warned his players against complacency.

items.h: Nigerian lecturer found dead in South Africa
items.s: Ayodele Odularu, 51, a Nigerian researcher at the University of Fort Hare, was found dead at her home in the Eastern Cape, South Africa. Her brother said she died on 16 August; relatives said they do not believe she died of natural causes, and an investigation is under way.

items.h: Unity college teachers suspend King's College strike
items.s: Teachers in the 117 federal unity colleges are expected back in class after the Association of Senior Civil Servants of Nigeria suspended its strike over the proposed concession of King's College, Lagos. The education ministry and labour agreed to put the concession on hold for two weeks while a seven-member committee reviews it.

items.h: 30 children rescued from illegal orphanage in Ilorin
items.s: The Kwara government rescued 30 children from an illegal orphanage in Ilorin on Thursday. The state chapter of the Association of Orphanages and Home Operators said it only identifies with registered homes that follow the social development ministry's guidelines.

items.h: Native doctor 'Eke Hit' jailed 12 years over money rituals
items.s: Justice Jude Obiora of the Anambra High Court in Awka sentenced native doctor Ekene Igboekweze, known as “Eke Hit”, to 12 years in prison on two counts, without the option of a fine. He and others were arraigned in April 2025 on charges including conspiracy, kidnapping, protective charms and money rituals.

items.h: Kano TikToker remanded over alleged defamation
items.s: Kano TikTok user Khadija Muhammad, known as Yar Lele, was remanded in a correctional centre after pleading not guilty at the Upper Shari'a Court in Kano Municipal to charges of defaming and insulting a politician, MD Hassan, with a derogatory expression.

items.h: Barau sacks aide over 'Abba Must Go' post
items.s: Deputy Senate President Barau Jibrin dismissed his aide Umar Alhassan, known as King Indara, over a social media post targeting Kano Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf, citing “indiscipline and disrespect” and anti-party conduct, his spokesman Shitu Madaki Kunchi said.

items.h: Police arrest suspected cult leader after Calabar shooting video
items.s: Police in Cross River arrested a suspected cult leader after a video circulated online showing a man firing shots from a moving vehicle in Calabar.

items.h: Delta police arrest seven suspected cultists
items.s: Delta police said their anti-kidnapping unit arrested seven suspected cultists on the Ghana Quarters–Umuebu road in Obiaruku on 13 September and recovered a gun and illicit drugs, spokesman Bright Edafe said.

items.h: Police commands pay insurance benefits to families of fallen officers
items.s: Lagos police commissioner Fatai Tijani presented insurance cheques worth N89.2 million to 157 families of officers who died in service, and the Oyo command gave cheques totalling about N37.9 million to 48 families, on behalf of the Inspector-General.

items.h: Police chiefs meet in Owerri on 2027 election security
items.s: The Nigeria Police Force will use its 2026 senior officers' conference and retreat in Owerri to develop strategies for securing the 2027 general elections, and Imo State said it expects economic and institutional benefits from hosting the event.

items.h: Ikeja Electric begins refunds for meters
items.s: Ikeja Electric began refunding customers who paid for meters under the Meter Asset Provider scheme, with refunds credited to their electricity purchases over an approved period, the company said at its monthly virtual stakeholder forum.

items.h: Reps intervene in NOUN law graduates' Law School admission
items.s: The House of Representatives intervened in the long-running impasse over the admission of National Open University of Nigeria law graduates to the Nigerian Law School, after affected graduates petitioned the House saying they had been denied bar training for years.

items.h: Olawepo-Hashim calls for INEC to be disbanded
items.s: Gbenga Olawepo-Hashim, Accord's presidential candidate, said INEC should be dissolved and rebuilt because it chose to appeal against, rather than obey, an appellate ruling that struck down four sections of the Electoral Act 2026 on party membership and nominations as unconstitutional.

items.h: Hamzat tells APC to campaign on facts
items.s: Lagos Deputy Governor Obafemi Hamzat, the APC's governorship candidate, told party members at the inauguration of the state campaign council to campaign on verifiable achievements and data rather than emotion. A support group congratulated him on his 62nd birthday.

items.h: Women's group starts nationwide drive for Tinubu
items.s: A group called Women of Influence for Tinubu 2027 began a nationwide campaign to rally women behind President Tinubu, saying it would use its networks in all 36 states and the FCT to promote the government's record.

items.h: Buratai launches book on his tenure
items.s: Former army chief Tukur Buratai thanked President Tinubu, service chiefs, traditional rulers and diplomats who attended the launch of “Military Transformational Leadership in Action: The Buratai Era”, a book on his tenure, at the Army Conference Centre in Abuja on 16 September.

items.h: Professor and daughter die in Sokoto gas explosion
items.s: Daily Trust told the story of the 9 September gas explosion at the Sokoto home of Professor Hassan Maishanu that killed him and his 21-year-old daughter Husnah, a first-year software engineering student. His 24-year-old wife, Zaliha, described a marriage of love and mutual respect cut short.

items.h: Jehovah's Witnesses relax blood rules
items.s: Jehovah's Witnesses will now leave it to each member's conscience whether to receive or donate the four primary components of blood, such as red cells, the movement's Governing Body announced from its headquarters in Warwick, New York, ending a strict ban the faith had held for decades.

items.h: Trump bars CNN, Politico and MS NOW from White House
items.s: President Donald Trump barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House, accusing them of reporting “fiction and lies”. MS NOW said its reporters were turned away from the grounds on Saturday as the administration enforced the ban.
